text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon II said in an interview for Italia's La Stampa he was ready to accept a four-year term to rule as a king to lead the country out of the crisis.

-- Bulgarian protesters kept on the blockade of the main road to Greece at the town of Doupnitsa. Protesters were also expected to block for one hour the main road to Turkey at Svilengrad on Friday. @

-- Bulgaria must restore political stability before any new aid package from international financial institutions could be considered, European Union's External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said.
-- Phone call charges in Bulgaria are expected to rise by 80 percent from March 1, the Post and Telecommunications Committee said.
-- Bulgaria's state gas supplier Bulgargas said it was reducing supplies of Russian gas to industrial plants which had not paid their January bills. @

-- The central bank said it had put in circulation new notes worth 6.9 billion levs in the first three days of this week alone to meet rising demand from Bulgarians who rushed to withdraw deposits from commercial banks because of the sharp lev fall against the dollar.
-- Bulgaria's State Railway Company said it would raise passenger tarriffs by 39 percent from tomorrow.
-- Some 230,000 Bulgarians on Thursday joined the national strike organised by trade unions with calls for early parliamentary elections, union officials said.
-- Bulgaria is likely to face hyperinflation in the next few months, the National Statistics Institute's chairman Zahari Karamfilov told a news conference.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing Foreign minister Georgi Pirinski called for an extraordinary congress of the ruling Socialist party to discuss changes in the party and ways out of the deepening economic crisis. @
